atoms.1: Dysphagia and dysarthria are common symptoms of neurological disorders affecting the cranial nerves or the brainstem.
atoms.2: Tongue fasciculations and difficulty with tongue movements suggest involvement of the lower motor neurons (LMNs).
atoms.3: Pronounced jaw jerk reflex indicates upper motor neuron (UMN) involvement.
atoms.4: The combination of UMN and LMN signs is characteristic of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
atoms.5: ALS is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects both UMNs and LMNs.
atoms.6: ALS leads to muscle weakness, atrophy, and fasciculations, along with exaggerated reflexes.
atoms.7: The absence of sensory deficits supports the diagnosis of ALS.
atoms.9: Baclofen is used primarily for muscle spasticity.
atoms.10: Baclofen may provide symptomatic relief in ALS.
atoms.11: Baclofen does not improve survival in ALS.
atoms.12: Dextromethorphan and Quinidine are used to treat pseudobulbar affect.
atoms.13: Dextromethorphan and Quinidine are a symptom management strategy.
atoms.14: Dextromethorphan and Quinidine do not improve survival in ALS.
atoms.15: Edaravone has been shown to slow the progression of ALS in specific patient populations.
atoms.16: Edaravone may modestly improve survival in ALS.
atoms.17: Riluzole is the standard treatment for ALS.
atoms.18: Riluzole has been shown to extend survival in patients with ALS.
atoms.19: Tizanidine is an antispastic agent used for muscle spasticity.
atoms.20: Tizanidine does not improve survival in ALS.
atoms.21: Given the diagnosis of ALS based on the patient’s symptoms and clinical findings, the therapy most likely to improve survival is Riluzole.
